title: Alignment Debt: The Hidden Work of Making AI Usable

bias_targets.methodology: A cross-sectional survey of 411 AI users in Kenya and Nigeria, mapping self-reported challenges such as accent and dialect misunderstanding, lack of cultural awareness, and perceived judgmental or biased tone.

A survey measuring self-reported user friction regarding slow response times and the need for stronger internet signals, evaluating the mismatch between AI design assumptions and local connectivity constraints.

Surveying users on their frequency of encountering wrong answers, misinformation, or a lack of source explanations, and measuring the resulting 'verification behavior' (propensity and intensity of cross-checking outputs) as a coping mechanism.
Surveying users on self-reported difficulties formulating prompts or being understood by LLMs, assessing the mismatch between Western-centric system interaction models and local user workflows.
